directAnswer: You can charge an EV from a normal socket using a standard Level 1 charger, which typically provides around 3-5 miles of range per hour of charging.
summary: Charging an electric vehicle (EV) from a standard household socket is possible but may take longer compared to dedicated charging stations.

sections.heading: Understanding Level 1 Charging
sections.body: Level 1 charging uses a standard 120V outlet, which is common in most homes. This method is slower than Level 2 charging but is convenient for overnight charging.

sections.heading: Safety Considerations
sections.body: Ensure that the outlet is in good condition and can handle the EV charger load. Avoid using extension cords, as they can overheat.

sections.heading: Charging Time
sections.body: Charging an EV from a normal socket can take 8-12 hours or longer, depending on the battery size and state of charge.

steps.title: Check Your Outlet
steps.detail: Ensure you have a standard 120V outlet available for charging.

steps.title: Connect the Charger
steps.detail: Plug the Level 1 charger into the outlet and connect the other end to your EV.

steps.title: Monitor Charging
steps.detail: Keep an eye on the charging status through your vehicle's dashboard or mobile app.

steps.title: Unplug After Charging
steps.detail: Once fully charged, unplug the charger from the vehicle and the outlet.

faqs.question: Can I use an extension cord for charging?
faqs.answer: It is not recommended to use an extension cord, as it can lead to overheating and potential fire hazards.

faqs.question: How long does it take to fully charge an EV from a normal socket?
faqs.answer: Charging time varies by vehicle but typically takes between 8 to 12 hours or more.

faqs.question: Is it safe to charge my EV overnight?
faqs.answer: Yes, charging overnight is common and safe as long as the outlet and charger are in good condition.

caveats: Charging from a normal socket is slower compared to dedicated EV chargers.
Ensure the electrical system can support the charging load.
